CRISIS COMMAND / FICTIONAL PRACTICE BRIEF

One cabinet.
One decision.

Two districts have lost their road connections after heavy rain. One has a clinic running low on supplies. In the other, families are waiting to leave. Your cabinet has one transport crew available before nightfall.

YOUR FIRST MOVE

Where do you send the crew?

Choose a response to see its consequence. There’s no score: the discussion starts with what your choice leaves unresolved.

Deliver supplies to the clinic

The clinic can keep treating patients overnight. Families in the second district must wait for transport.

Your cabinet asks: what can you offer those families before the next crew arrives?
Evacuate families first

The first group reaches shelter. The clinic still needs supplies, and the road may remain closed tomorrow.

Your cabinet asks: how will you decide who gets a seat on the first trip?
Clear the road to reopen both routes

A repaired crossing could serve both districts tomorrow. Neither receives immediate help tonight.

Your cabinet asks: what evidence would make you abandon the repair and switch plans?

Want to make the next decision with your team?
